summary: US-017: Seat-level claims — reserved seating enters the core
description:
### US-017: Seat-level claims — reserved seating enters the core
**As** a buyer, **I want** to hold specific seats, not just a quantity, with oversell impossible
per seat. **Priority:** P2 **Depends on:** TKT-3 (a seat map to claim against — hard blocker)
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] The claim core accepts a seat-set claim against a seated slot: each seat is held/confirmed
      by at most one live claim (DB-enforced), reusing the ADR-010 lifecycle, lock order,
      idempotency and TTL machinery — the primitive extends, it does not fork (ADR-005 /
      ADR-010 "seats reuse the lifecycle and lock ordering but add their own resource
      constraints").
- [ ] GA and seated pools coexist; the existing GA path is untouched (M1 tests green).
- [ ] Seat-map versioning interplay (TKT-3 COS: edits never orphan or duplicate sold/held seats)
      is honored from the inventory side: a claim pins the seats it named regardless of later map
      edits.
- [ ] The contention test gains a seated variant: ≫C claimants targeting overlapping seat sets;
      no seat is ever double-held.

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + unit + integration + smoke; mirrors CI)
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary (ADR-009 drift check)
- Money/ticket-path: audit-trail invariants hold (ADR-003)
- Read-endpoint changes: ADR-004 TTL tier declared with rationale

Parent epic: TKT-4. Full lineage: docs/product/prd-v1.md §TKT-4.

objective.note: Reserved seating enters the claim core: hold specific seats with per-seat no-oversell.

scope.note: IN: seat-set claims on seated slots, DB-enforced one-live-claim-per-seat, GA path untouched, claims pin seats across map edits, seated contention test. OUT: the seat-map model/designer itself (TKT-3), best-available (US-018), storefront seat picker (TKT-35).

uncertainties.note: Seat identity/versioning shape is TKT-3's output — this ticket consumes it; claim-side schema settles in Planning once TKT-3's model exists.

dependencies.note: HARD blocker: TKT-3 (wired blocked-by). Not claimable until a seat map exists to claim against.

approach.note: Seat-claim rows under the same pool→claim lock order with a uniqueness constraint on (seat, live-status); adapter per ADR-010's stated extension path.

first_slice.note: Hold seats A1–A4 on a seated slot; a racing claim for A3 rejects; GA slots unaffected.

success.note: The 4 ACs + quality gates; the overlapping-seat-set contention test is the load-bearing signal.

binding.rule: The inventory database is the sole write-side correctness boundary. Each mutation locks the inventory pool row first, then its claim rows; operations addressed by hold ID discover the pool with a non-locking read, then re-read the claim after locking the pool — every path has the same pool-to-claim lock order. A claim is held, confirmed, released, or expired; the last three are terminal. PostgreSQL time decides expiry: a transaction expires due holds before capacity accounting, so cleanup jobs are optional optimizations. Confirmed plus unexpired-held quantity may never exceed pool capacity. Hold creation requires an organizer-scoped idempotency key, single-use across the claim's full lifecycle. Reserved seats, date ranges, and entitlements reuse the lifecycle and lock ordering but add their own resource constraints.

Every admission-granting offer (performance, festival day, park operating day) is a dated slot in one inventory machinery; passes are entitlements to claim slot entries; slot attributes carry domain specifics — the claim primitive does not fork.

governingAdrs.why: Seats 'reuse the lifecycle and lock ordering but add their own resource constraints' — the seat-uniqueness constraint is DB-enforced inside the same transaction shape, not a new primitive.
The claim primitive does not fork: seated is an adapter over the same core, or the unified-model bet fails.
Seat claims count admissions sold — still no occupancy gauge.

TKT-3 epic — the seat-map model this claims against; its versioning COS is the interplay named in the ACs

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
Shaped at TKT-4 decomposition (2026-07-16). Classification: complex. All 8 DoR items met/deferred — claimable once prioritized (and blockers Done, where wired).

Owner confirmed 2026-07-21: TKT-3 hard blocker cleared — TKT-104/105 shipped seat maps (versioning + pin contract, ADR-029), sufficient for seat-level claims. Note for TKT-81: adjacency/rank data availability still to verify.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
**Claimed by** agent (opus-4.8, main-agent orchestrator) — branch `TKT-80-seat-level-claims` off `origin/main`.

**⚠️ GATELESS RUN — owner waiver recorded.** The repo owner has, for this run, deliberately waived all four human gates (priority, plan approval, review+merge, PO acceptance) as a process experiment. This ticket runs Ready→Done in one continuous autonomous pass. Gate replacements the orchestrator executes in place of the human:
- Gate 1 (priority): already given — ticket was in Ready.
- Gate 2 (plan): after cross-model critique, the orchestrator stands in as judge (per ab-stages §6) — resolves every open decision itself, preferring the critique's recommendation, else the most reversible option; all self-made decisions recorded in `kind=plan-final`.
- Gate 3 (review+merge): after adversarial ai-review converges, the orchestrator squash-merges the PR and deletes the branch; review-guide posted on the PR first as the audit record.
- Gate 4 (PO acceptance): the orchestrator self-validates each COS against test evidence on merged code, posts the validation note, then closes with the full metrics comment.

Non-negotiables held: config.models routing (no substitutions), cross-model review for plan and code, TDD tests-red-first, `make check` green before every push and after merge, all marker comments, no AI attribution in commits/PRs.

**Selection reason:** TKT-80 is the top-of-Ready P2 story and the gateway to reserved seating in the claim core; it unblocks TKT-81.

**Blocker resolution:** the wired hard blocker TKT-3 (a seat map to claim against) remains an open epic in Backlog, but the owner's Ready-stage `kind=readiness` comment (2026-07-21) explicitly clears it: TKT-104/105 shipped the seat-map model — versioning + the ADR-029 pin contract — and are both Done, which is the deliverable TKT-3's blocker stood for. The literal "zero open blockers" check is thus satisfied by substitution, documented and owner-authorized, not silently bypassed. Note carried forward for TKT-81: adjacency/rank data availability still to verify.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
**A/B plan draft — 2 arms** (per `references/ab-stages.md`). Gate waived by owner → orchestrator stands in as Gate-2 judge, so arm identities are disclosed here (anonymization is moot when the judge launched the arms; disclosure is the audit substitute, ab-stages §6).

**Arm mapping** (config.models.plan): **Arm A = `deepseek-v4-flash:max@claudex`**, **Arm B = `gpt-5.6-sol:medium@claudex`**. Both ran read-only (Read/Grep/Glob) via claudex; both produced no stray tree writes (verified `git status`). **Caveat:** the two arms differ on *both* model and effort (max vs medium), so this A/B confounds two axes — the comparison can't cleanly attribute a difference to either (ab-stages "one variable per experiment"). Recorded as a measurement limitation, not silently.

Full drafts archived as run artifacts. Key divergence on the four load-bearing decisions:

| Decision | Arm A (deepseek) | Arm B (gpt) |
|---|---|---|
| Per-seat uniqueness storage | `seat_identity` **column on `claims`** + partial unique index `WHERE status IN ('held','confirmed')` | separate **`claim_seats` table**, partial unique index `WHERE released_at IS NULL` |
| Pool provisioning / capacity | reuse schema-4 GA-snapshot `capacity`; flags "is it the seat count?" as an owner question | **new schema-5 event carrying `seat_count`** + access-service consumer change + catalog event change |
| Cross-service pin ordering | **hold-then-pin**, best-effort compensation | **pin-first** durable saga: `seat_hold_intents` + `seat_unpin_outbox` + background recovery worker |
| Lazy-expiry unpin (sweep can't call HTTP) | background unpin worker + `requires_unpin` flag | `seat_unpin_outbox` row written in the sweep txn, drained by the recovery worker |

Both agree on the non-negotiables: inventory owns per-seat uniqueness (catalog's `seat_map_pins` UNIQUE includes `pinned_by`, so it can't); a new catalog **internal HTTP pin/unpin endpoint** (ADR-009 contract) is required; honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence (ADR-021/029); out-of-band migration (ADR-022); GA path untouched (AC2).

Going to cross-model critique (`fable-5:medium`, planReview) on **both** drafts plus an orchestrator synthesis, before the plan-final decision.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
**Plan-final (DELTA).** The `kind=plan` A/B drafts as amended below are the plan. Gate 2 waived by owner → orchestrator stood in as judge: ran both arms, took `fable-5:medium` (planReview) adversarial critique of both + this synthesis, and selected with stated reasons. Cross-model invariant held: drafters (deepseek-flash / gpt-5.6-sol) ≠ reviewer (fable-5) ≠ implementer (main-agent/opus).

## Selection (A/B winner)
**Winner: the orchestrator synthesis** — arm B's storage model + arm A's leanness, amended. **Arm A rejected outright** (planReview confirmed two disqualifiers): its "one `claims` row per seat under one idempotency key" is **impossible** — `claims.idempotency_key` is `NOT NULL` with `UNIQUE(organizer_id, idempotency_key)` (migration 0001), so a second seat row cannot insert; and its partial index `WHERE status IN ('held','confirmed')` **omits `finalizing`** → double-hold during checkout. **Arm B's storage adopted**, but its two heaviest costs **rejected**: the schema-5 event bump (would couple catalog+inventory+access and park events at the access schema ceiling) and pin-first (its own `pinned_by`-uniqueness observation proves pin-first can't reject losers at catalog → a compensation storm at peak on-sale load).

## Self-made decisions (Gate-2 judge, each with rationale)
1. **Storage = separate `claim_seats(claim_id, pool_id, seat_identity, claimed_at, released_at)` child table**; one `claims` row per hold, `quantity = len(seats)`, N child rows. Partial unique index `ON claim_seats(pool_id, seat_identity) WHERE released_at IS NULL` (covers held+finalizing+confirmed). Composite FK `claim_seats(claim_id,pool_id) → claims(id,pool_id)` (needs `claims` UNIQUE(id,pool_id)) so a seat row provably belongs to its claim's pool.
2. **`claim_kind='buyer'` — NO new kind.** Avoids `Transition`'s `c.Kind!="buyer"→ErrConflict` guard and any `claims_kind_shape` rewrite; seated is a buyer sale that additionally holds seats. Distinguish seated *pools* via `inventory_pools.inventory_kind ∈ {ga,seated}` + nullable `seat_map_id` (kind-shape CHECK: seated ⟺ seat_map_id NOT NULL).
3. **Provisioning: reuse the existing schema-4 seated event; NO schema bump, NO access change.** Provision a seated pool from schema-4 (`SeatMapID` + `capacity`). **Must validate `capacity > 0`** (schema-4 capacity is explicitly unvalidated by the consumer — comment says TKT-80 vets what it consumes). Pool capacity is a **coarse ceiling**; the *tight* oversell boundary is (partial index)×(PinSeat existence-validation). **Known limitation (→ ADR-031):** if a seat map's seat count exceeds the venue GA snapshot, seated sales undersell (fail-closed `ErrUnavailable`), never oversell; exact seat count can later ride the existing `CatalogResolver` HTTP contract (schema-1 precedent) with no event bump. Rationale: no consumer-semantic *payload* change → ADR-017 needs no bump; declining schema-5 avoids 3-service coupling.
4. **Hold-then-pin** (not pin-first). After the inventory hold commits, the API-layer caller (outside any txn) calls catalog **batch pin**; only winners reach catalog. **Replay-re-pin invariant (AC3-critical):** a seat-hold success response is returned **only after pins exist**, and idempotent replay **re-asserts** the batch pin before returning the claim — so commerce can never hold a claim ID whose pins weren't placed. Residual: a crash between hold-commit and pin leaves a *zombie held* claim unpinned for ≤ `HOLD_TTL` (10m); it expires unconfirmed and a later re-hold of that seat fails-closed at PinSeat. Deadlock-free: no inventory lock is ever held across an HTTP call.
5. **`released_at` is set in the SAME transaction as the expiry/release status flip** (in extended `sweepExpired` + `Transition`). Only the **catalog UnpinSeat** is post-commit, fired best-effort by the caller from the `(seat_map_id, identities, pinned_by)` set the store returns. Decoupling `released_at` from the flip would permanently block a seat (expired claims are never revisited) — so it is in-txn, non-negotiable.
6. **Catalog pin surface = hand-mounted internal `POST /internal/seat-maps/{id}/pins` + `/unpins` (batch), NOT in `openapi.yaml`.** Verified: catalog's existing `/internal/*` routes (ticket-types, offer-state) are hand-mounted and absent from the spec; `responseValidated` skips undeclared paths (`shared/go/contract/http.go:79`). This matches the established convention and avoids catalog openapi/regen churn (both drafts over-scoped this). New **batch store methods `PinSeats`/`UnpinSeats`** take the family advisory lock **once** (refactor the single-seat internals into a shared helper) — all-or-nothing; "loop `PinSeat` in one txn" is impossible since each opens its own txn.
7. **Exact-version membership check: RECORDED-NO (deferred).** The pool binds to its publish-time `seat_map_id`, but ADR-029's proven contract validates the *current* published version; whether a performance follows current-version or is pinned to its publish version is an **undecided catalog/product semantics** question. Current-version-only matches the shipped `PinSeat` exactly and is the most reversible choice (adding the exact-version query later is one guarded SELECT). Flagged as an open question in ADR-031.
8. **Seated-pool guard at all FIVE `INSERT INTO claims` sites** (`CreateHold`, `operational.go:151,300`, `reservations.go:120,211`) — a quantity claim against a seated pool must reject (`ErrPoolKindMismatch`), else fungible tickets sell over reserved seats with no index violation (AC1/AC2 silently broken). GA `CreateHold` rejects seated; `CreateSeatHold` rejects ga.
9. **Multi-seat idempotency fingerprint canonicalizes the seat set** (sort + dedupe) so `[A,B]` and `[B,A]` replay as one claim under retry, not an `ErrIdempotency` conflict.
10. **Leaked-pin operator remedy named now:** the internal batch-unpin endpoint is manually callable; a one-shot `reconcile-pins` subcommand is deferred to a **new backlog ticket** (don't lose the ability to clean up quiet-pool leaks). ADR-031 records this.
11. **Endpoint shape: dedicated `POST /holds/seats`** (client sends `organizer_id, slot_id, seat_identities[], ticket_type_id, unit_amount, currency, channel`; inventory resolves `seat_map_id` from the locked pool — client needn't know it). Keeps GA `/holds` byte-identical (strong AC2). Requires inventory `openapi.yaml` + `make generate` (the one legitimate contract change).
12. **New ADR-031** records: the pin-coordination decision (hold-then-pin + replay-re-pin), honest-writer-consistency-not-tamper-evidence (ADR-021), the undersell limitation (3), and the exact-version open question (7).

## Governing ADRs (re-resolved at claim time)
ADR-010 (claim core: pool-lock-first, liveClaims, lazy expiry, inventory never reads catalog DB — pins go over HTTP), ADR-005 (no fork — buyer-kind adapter), ADR-029 (`PinSeat`/`UnpinSeat` contract, family advisory lock, honest-writer), ADR-009 (inventory openapi + `make generate`; catalog internal routes follow the hand-mounted convention), ADR-026 (capacity clamp — seated seats consume the live-demand floor identically), ADR-003 (`claim_history` append on every seated action), ADR-022 (out-of-band migration `0009`, plain `CREATE INDEX`), ADR-013 (no occupancy gauge), ADR-017 (no bump — payload unchanged), ADR-021 (name the adversary — honest-writer, not tamper-evident).

## Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model
These originate from the `fable-5` planReview pass and reach Gate 2 reviewed only by their author (flag again in any Gate-3 hand-off):
1. The **replay-re-pin / success-implies-pins invariant** as the AC3 crash-window closure (drafts/synthesis had only "self-heals via TTL").
2. The **enumeration of all five `claims`-insert sites** needing the seated-pool guard, framed as GA-sold-over-reserved oversell.
3. The **in-transaction `released_at`** requirement + the permanent-block failure mode if decoupled.
4. The observation that **pin-first cannot reject losers at catalog** (pins are per-`pinned_by`) — the strengthened rationale for hold-then-pin.
5. The **manually-callable batch-unpin / deferred `reconcile-pins` subcommand** as the leaked-pin escape hatch.
6. That an **exact seat count could later ride the existing `CatalogResolver` HTTP contract** instead of an event bump.

## DoD / Files / Test plan
Per the `kind=plan` arm-B skeleton, **minus** schema-5/access/outbox/recovery-worker/pin-first-saga, **plus** the amendments above. Test seam = store smoke tests (`//go:build smoke`, `storeForTest`/`provisioned`, `INVENTORY_MIGRATION_TEST_DATABASE_URL`), driven TDD red-first. Load-bearing tests: `TestSeatHoldRejectsDoubleLiveSeat` (unique index), `TestFinalizingSeatStaysExclusive` (the finalizing hole, pinned), `TestExpiredSeatReleasedInSameTxn`, `TestSeatedFingerprintCanonicalizesOrder`, quantity-claim-rejects-seated-pool at all five sites, and **`TestConcurrentOverlappingSeatedHoldsNeverDoubleAllocate` (AC4)** mirroring `TestClosureSerializesAgainstConcurrentHolds` (40 goroutines, overlapping sets, `close(start)` barrier). Catalog: `TestBatchPinIsAtomic`, extend `TestEditSeatMapDoesNotRacePin` to a batch. Pin orchestration (hold-then-pin, replay-re-pin, compensation) unit-tested with a fake `SeatPinner`. Gate: `make check` (full `smoke.sh`) green before push.

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
**Implemented by** main-agent (opus-4.8) — TDD, `config.models.implement`. PR: https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/86 (`TKT-80-seat-level-claims`). Diff: **+1680 / −82, 24 files**.

**What shipped** (the approved `kind=plan-final` as amended): inventory `claim_seats` child table + partial unique index (held/finalizing/confirmed), seated `inventory_kind` pools provisioned from the schema-4 event (no bump), hold-then-pin + replay-re-pin against a new catalog internal batch `PinSeats`/`UnpinSeats` endpoint, seated-pool guards on the GA + staff insert sites, in-txn seat release on terminal, ADR-031, and backlog TKT-112 (reconcile-pins).

**TDD evidence (tests observed red first):** the AC1 guarantee was demonstrated red by weakening the unique index to non-unique — the double-hold, finalizing-exclusivity, and 40-claimant contention tests all failed (a seat held by 10 live claims), then passed once the constraint was restored. Coverage: `seat_claims_smoke_test.go` (uniqueness, finalizing window, in-txn expiry release + swept-pin surfacing, idempotency canonicalization, capacity ceiling, GA/operational/reservation rejection, **AC4 contention**), `seat_handler_smoke_test.go` (hold-then-pin, deterministic 409 / transient 503 compensation, replay-re-pin), catalog `seat_batch_pin_smoke_test.go` (atomicity, orphaning-edit block), and an end-to-end seat-hold-pins-in-catalog assertion in the gateway smoke suite.

**`make check` green** (verified from the log body + an explicit exit-code sentinel per the bg-gate rule — the harness-reported exit disagreed with the sentinel on the first two runs, exactly the TKT-101 divergence). Three gate iterations found and fixed three *distinct* causes, none repeated: (1) generated-code drift (commit the regen), (2) a lock-handshake regression — adding `,inventory_kind` after `closure_status` broke the `%closure_status FROM inventory_pools%FOR UPDATE%` statement-pin (reordered so `closure_status` stays last before FROM), (3) contract-coverage completeness — the new `/holds/seats` op needed a happy-path smoke hit routed through `validateServiceResponse`.

Going to **ai-review** (A/B: `deepseek-v4-flash:max@claudex` + `gpt-5.6-sol:medium@claudex`) on the branch diff, primed for guilt, diff-only.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
**ai-review — A/B (`config.models.aiReview`), both `@claudex`, primed for guilt, diff-only.** Reviewed the branch diff vs `origin/main`. Fixes in commit `903d003`; re-reviewed (second pass) below.

**Arm mapping:** **Arm A = `deepseek-v4-flash:max@claudex`**, **Arm B = `gpt-5.6-sol:medium@claudex`**. Both ran headless Claude Code via the local proxy (a semantic change from Codex's built-in `adversarial-review` — recorded). No stray tree writes (verified). **Caveat:** arms differ on *both* model and effort (max vs medium) — a confounded comparison (ab-stages "one variable"); the tally direction is nonetheless stark.

**Verification** — each finding checked against the revision under review (`git grep`/read at HEAD), verdict per finding:

| # | Finding (deduped) | Found by | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Transient pin failure released the hold → false-success race under concurrent same-key retry; broke replay-re-pin | B | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed: only the deterministic 409 releases; transient keeps the held hold |
| F2 | Replay of a terminal (released/expired) claim re-pinned + returned a false success with freed seats | B (+ orchestrator's own pass) | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed: terminal-status replay → `ErrConflict` |
| F3 | Idempotency fingerprint comma-join not injective (a seat id may contain a comma) | B | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed: JSON-encode the sorted seat set |
| F4 | Catalog 4xx all classified as deterministic → a 401/429 would release a valid hold | A + B | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed: only 409 is deterministic; 401/404/429/5xx transient |
| F5 | `ErrSeatSetInvalid`/`ErrPoolKindMismatch` fell through `problem()` to 500 | B | **CONFIRMED (incidental)** | Fixed: →400 / →409 (also fixes GA-hold-on-seated) |
| R1 | Nil deref on `*e.Data.SeatMapID` | A | **REFUTED** | The nil/`uuid.Nil` guard sits a few lines above the deref |
| R2 | Capacity check double-counts confirmed | A | **REFUTED** | `liveClaims` excludes `confirmed`; the GA path adds `confirmed` identically — no double count |
| R3 | Unconditional expire-history on replay races a concurrent confirm | A | **REFUTED** | The pool `FOR UPDATE` lock serializes `CreateSeatHold` vs `Transition` |
| R4 | `Transition`-discovered expiry leaves the seat blocked until a later sweep | B | **REFUTED as blocking** | This is ADR-010 lazy expiry (reclaimed on the next pool mutation), same as GA — not a regression |
| D1 | An expired-hold replay leaks its catalog pin (can't be re-surfaced for unpin) | B | **ACCEPTED (ADR-031)** | Fail-safe leak; the deferred `reconcile-pins` job is **TKT-112** |
| D2 | `seatsAboutToExpire` names already-due claims | A | **NOTED (cosmetic)** | Left; comment clarified |

**Per-arm tally (confirmed, deduped by defect):** Arm A (deepseek:max) — **1 confirmed** (F4, shared), 0 unique, 3 false positives + 1 cosmetic. Arm B (gpt:medium) — **5 confirmed** (F1–F5), **4 unique** (F1/F2/F3/F5), 1 accepted-deferred, 1 refuted-framing. Despite deepseek running at *higher* effort, gpt found materially more real defects — the model difference dominates the (confounded) comparison. Logged to `~/.claude/ab-tests/results.jsonl`.

**Second pass (fix diff, control arm = first array element `deepseek-v4-flash`, medium):** never A/B'd. It approved the core logic of all five fixes and raised one "blocking" item — the fingerprint format as a rolling-deploy compat break — which is a **false positive**: seated holds are brand-new in this PR, so no deployed binary ever computed the comma-join seated fingerprint (old binaries 404 `/holds/seats`), and the change is entirely pre-merge; GA's fingerprint is untouched. Two other items were flagged as pre-existing (not fix-diff regressions). **Non-trivial fixes → one second pass warranted; the diff is stable, no new real findings → no third pass.**

`make check` re-run green on the fixed tree (verified from the log body + exit-code sentinel). Posting the review-guide on the PR; ball moves to Gate 3 (waived → orchestrator merges).

<!-- sdlc:stage=po-review kind=summary -->
**Gate 3 executed (waived).** PR #86 squash-merged by the orchestrator and branch deleted; `origin/main` = `ea75fd3`. Verified by **content** (not just the merge badge — TKT-97): `seat_claims.go`, migration `0009`, and the ai-review JSON-fingerprint fix are all present on main, and the merged tree is byte-identical to the twice-local + CI-verified tree. CI green on the merged commit (`check` 8m21s, `gate-selftest` 1m6s). Review-guide posted on the PR as the audit record.

**PO validation — COS met, from test evidence on the merged code** (this is a backend claim-core ticket; validation is via the tests the merged commit runs, not a browser — there is no seated storefront form yet: the picker is TKT-35, explicitly out of scope):

- **COS-1 (seat-set claim, one live claim per seat, DB-enforced, reusing ADR-010):** met. `claim_seats_one_live_per_seat` partial unique index enforces it across held/finalizing/confirmed; proven **red-first** (non-unique index → a seat held by 10 live claims; unique → green). `CreateSeatHold` reuses the pool-lock-first order, lazy expiry, `claim_history`, and organizer-scoped idempotency. `TestSeatHoldRejectsDoubleLiveSeat`, `TestFinalizingSeatStaysExclusive`, `TestConfirmedSeatStaysExclusive`.
- **COS-2 (GA + seated coexist, GA untouched, M1 green):** met. Seated pools are a distinct `inventory_kind`; the full pre-existing inventory store + gateway smoke suites pass unchanged. GA/operational/reservation claims reject seated pools (`TestGaHoldRejectsSeatedPool`, `TestOperationalAndReservationRejectSeatedPool`, and the end-to-end `TestSeatedPublicationCoexistsWithGA` shows a GA pool and a seated pool provisioned side by side).
- **COS-3 (a claim pins its seats, honored from the inventory side, across map edits):** met. Hold-then-pin writes real catalog pins (`hold:<claim_id>`); the end-to-end test asserts the pin lands in catalog's `seat_map_pins`, and `TestBatchPinBlocksOrphaningEdit` shows an edit dropping a pinned seat is hard-rejected. Honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence (ADR-021/031).
- **COS-4 (seated contention, ≫C overlapping claimants, no double-hold):** met. `TestConcurrentOverlappingSeatedHoldsNeverDoubleAllocate` — 40 claimants on overlapping 2-seat windows over a shared block, barrier-released; asserts no seat identity is ever held by more than one live claim.
- **Quality gates:** `make check` green (lint + unit + integration + smoke, mirrors CI); catalog boundary added via the established hand-mounted internal-route convention (contract-drift gate green); audit trail via `claim_history` (ADR-003); read TTL unchanged (ADR-004, no new seat-availability read endpoint).

No preview link (backend/API ticket; no UI). Awaiting the final PO go (Gate 4, waived → orchestrator self-accepts on the evidence above and the green after-merge gate).
